observations.statement: WM-001 is an accepted generated-artifact residual whose active source-preserving product coverage is retired to migration-lineage-only compatibility; fine-grained PlanUnits or explicit structural/reference dispositions carry the earlier product coverage.
WM-001 uses source_preserving_bridge_retired compile mode with WorkNode creation disabled, and its acceptance criteria prohibit creation of executable or implementation artifacts.
Migration coverage records one original hash and four run-scoped proof artifacts for original hashes, span mapping, coverage mapping, and anchor aliases.

Phase 2B batch 201 dispositioned S0044 through S0047, retired WM-001, removed active source_preserving_planunit coverage, and explicitly did not refresh governance artifacts or create runtime, build, implementation, or source-code artifacts.

WM-036 consolidates recovery, blocked/unblocked, safe-point, remediation, canonical-event-row, and recovery-action-binding addenda into explicit producer/consumer/action PlanUnits and gives named PlanUnits plus Contracts_V0 event identities precedence over adjacent addendum order.

WM-036 depends on WM-012 through WM-017, preserves event/action tokens for node and wizard blocking, attempts, graph integrity, safe points, remediation, and allowed_action_id, and keeps Wiring_Matrix from replacing Contracts_V0 event identity or Executor scheduler ownership.
WM-037 maps Goal button/chip/icon activation and /goal to cmd.chat.goal.start, and maps the Goal status update icon, /goal again, and natural-language update requests to cmd.chat.goal.update.

WM-037 is GUI-related because it wires user-visible Goal controls, while command execution targets the Goal Runtime controller and concrete Goal event payload schema ownership remains outside Wiring_Matrix.

WM-038 requires Approve And Build to atomically write the immutable pack, approval receipt, and PlanApproved transactional-outbox event so approval cannot commit without a recoverable downstream trigger.
WM-038 specifies a deterministic PlanApproved idempotency key derived from project_id, pack_id, pack version, and pack hash, with duplicate delivery returning the existing PlanCompileRun.

After provisioning acceptance, WM-038 requires one activation transaction to create or bind a GoalRun in activating state, install a certified WorkGraph revision, materialize WorkNodes, queue runnable entrypoints, record an activation receipt, and outbox GoalRunStarted or BuildStarted.

WM-038 enumerates planning command families and requires permission, enablement, disabled reason, idempotency, stale-projection behavior, receipt effect, and recovery to be defined, followed by a broad doc-impact pass.
WM-038 is classified GUI-related, but this ledger-to-Plans compile is explicitly source-lineage-only and has WorkNode and NodeSeed creation disabled.

candidate_findings.title: WM-036 lacks an explicit behavioral wiring oracle
candidate_findings.statement: WM-036 acceptance requires runtime wiring precedence across several behavior classes, but its validation surfaces name only the plan-index validator and bootstrap-ledger validator; the assigned core specifies no event-by-event producer/consumer/action fixture or assertion that proves the required routing and precedence.
candidate_findings.impact: A structurally valid index or ledger could leave incorrect runtime routing or precedence undetected.

candidate_findings.title: WM-037 wiring validation is deferred to an undefined future surface
candidate_findings.statement: The only routing-specific validation entry for WM-037 is the literal placeholder future wiring coverage validation; no executable command, fixture, artifact, or expected assertion is identified for the start and update mappings.
candidate_findings.impact: The exact GUI-to-command mappings can be implemented incorrectly without a specified acceptance oracle in this window.

candidate_findings.title: Natural-language Goal update recognition is unspecified
candidate_findings.statement: WM-037 routes natural-language update requests to cmd.chat.goal.update but does not define recognition criteria, ambiguity handling, confirmation behavior, or the start-versus-update state preconditions for that producer.
candidate_findings.impact: Different builders can classify the same user utterance differently or dispatch an update against an invalid Goal state.

candidate_findings.title: Goal command control-plane behavior is absent from the wiring contract
candidate_findings.statement: WM-037 defines producer-to-command routing and an ownership boundary, but the assigned core does not state permission, enablement, disabled-reason, idempotency, retry, rejection, error-receipt, or cancellation behavior for cmd.chat.goal.start or cmd.chat.goal.update.
candidate_findings.impact: User-visible failure behavior and duplicate-command handling remain consequential builder choices unless another owner contract supplies them.

candidate_findings.title: PlanApproved idempotency-key derivation is not interoperably specified
candidate_findings.statement: WM-038 names the four source fields for a deterministic idempotency key but does not define field types, normalization, ordering/encoding, separators, hash algorithm, namespace/versioning, or invalid/missing-field handling; the preserved token idempotency_key does not add those semantics.
candidate_findings.impact: Independent producers and consumers can derive different keys for the same approval, defeating deduplication or collapsing distinct approvals.

candidate_findings.title: Activation branch selection and conflict recovery are ambiguous
candidate_findings.statement: WM-038 requires the activation transaction to create or bind a GoalRun and to write GoalRunStarted or BuildStarted, but it does not define the branch-selection rules, the compatibility checks for binding an existing run, or the outcome when graph installation, node materialization, queueing, receipt recording, or outbox writing conflicts or fails.
candidate_findings.impact: Implementations can choose different run identities, event identities, and recovery outcomes for the same accepted provisioning result.

candidate_findings.title: The planning command contract matrix is asserted but not instantiated
candidate_findings.statement: WM-038 says the listed commands define permission, enablement, disabled reason, idempotency, stale-projection behavior, receipt effect, and recovery, yet the assigned core provides no stable command IDs or per-command values, state transitions, receipts, stale-version rules, or recovery actions; its negative_constraints list is empty.
candidate_findings.impact: Destructive and lifecycle-affecting commands such as approve, pause, cancel, resume, retry, and bounded recompile retain substantial inconsistent builder discretion.

candidate_findings.title: WM-038 declares no PlanUnit dependencies despite multi-owner behavior
candidate_findings.statement: WM-038 has depends_on: [] even though its canonical behavior invokes pack approval, PlanCompileRun, GoalRun, WorkGraph, Executor-facing queueing, command, GUI, contract, and cross-document obligations across eleven implementation surfaces and eleven owner hints.
candidate_findings.impact: Plan ordering and node-readiness analysis cannot express the prerequisite owner contracts needed to implement this wiring safely.

candidate_findings.title: WM-038 operational behavior lacks acceptance evidence
candidate_findings.statement: WM-038 acceptance criteria prove source-atom preservation, token retention, and non-creation during compile, while its validators cover the plan index and bootstrap ledger; no specified acceptance surface exercises approval atomicity, idempotent duplicate delivery, activation transaction effects, GoalRun state, outbox selection, or command recovery behavior.
candidate_findings.impact: The PlanUnit can satisfy its declared checks while its highest-risk transactional and lifecycle obligations remain unverified.

candidate_findings.title: The required doc-impact pass has no completion oracle
candidate_findings.statement: WM-038 requires a doc-impact pass over a broad set of product and governance domains, but the assigned core defines no output artifact, per-domain coverage rule, adjudication process, owner sign-off, or validation condition for completing that pass.
candidate_findings.impact: Cross-owner impacts can be silently missed while the PlanUnit still meets its listed acceptance criteria.

explicit_non_gaps.statement: WM-001's retirement boundary is explicit: it must not provide product implementation coverage, must not override WM-002 through WM-035 or later fine-grained units, and cannot remain the final coarse implementation standard.
WM-001 explicitly preserves malformed trailing-apostrophe ContractRef material as lineage only and does not promote it as active ContractRefs.
WM-036 explicitly resolves the authority boundary: Wiring_Matrix remains a wiring-row owner and does not replace Contracts_V0 event identity or Executor scheduler ownership.
WM-036 explicitly prohibits using adjacent addendum order as precedence and prohibits making Wiring_Matrix a general runtime schema owner.
WM-037's GUI producers, stable start/update command IDs, Goal Runtime target, and concrete-payload-schema ownership boundary are explicit.

WM-038 explicitly makes approval, immutable-pack persistence, approval-receipt persistence, and PlanApproved outbox persistence atomic so approval cannot commit without a recoverable downstream trigger.
WM-038 explicitly enumerates the idempotency-key input set and specifies that duplicate delivery returns the existing PlanCompileRun rather than creating another run.

The compile boundary is explicit for both ledger addenda: compiling source-lineage obligations does not itself create WorkNodes, NodeSeeds, executable queues, GoalRuns, implementation files, generated governance artifacts, or production build tasks.

unknowns.statement: The assigned window states but cannot independently establish whether WM-002 through WM-035 and the cited structural/reference dispositions completely cover every earlier Wiring_Matrix source span.

The exact producer, consumer, action, ordering, failure, and payload details supplied by WM-012 through WM-017 and Contracts_V0 cannot be determined from this window because WM-036 delegates precedence to those PlanUnits and event identities.

The Goal Runtime event-envelope shape and lifecycle, permission, rejection, and failure rules cannot be determined from this window because WM-037 targets that controller while explicitly declining concrete Goal payload-schema ownership.

The data types and validation rules for project_id, pack_id, pack version, pack hash, the immutable pack, approval receipt, activation receipt, and the returned PlanCompileRun are not defined in the assigned core.

Whether the declared migration, plan-index, and ledger validation commands currently pass is unknown; this blind document-window review records the named surfaces but does not execute repo-wide validators.
